pages.title: Historical 0.2.3 Interaction Polish
pages.intro: Historical 0.2.3 / Android code 6 record: 142 EditMode and 40 PlayMode tests passed and both APKs were built. This does not verify 0.2.5. Read InteractionStages.json for current hand presentation and station controls; the valve tap fallback below is superseded.

blocks.text: System hand aim and contextual feedback

Camp, settings, quit confirmation, HUD and shop use the shared system-defined hand pointer through MetaShadowPlayer.ReadInteractionAim. The existing filtered PICO fallback remains in the shared provider. Aim is not reconstructed from the curling index fingertip. A cyan ray and cursor appear only over an eligible, in-view UI target; leaving that target hides them. Existing SDK ray visual writers are suppressed without disabling tracking or input interactors. Same-hand fresh pinch and exclusive UI ownership remain required; head tracking still places the menu.

Short numbered cues and a marker identify pickup, matching the blue rings, holding still, operating the valve, filling, and taking the tool. Creek cues distinguish intake pickup, water placement, outward pull and return. The nearby coupling guide adjusts orientation around the current grip contact; it neither moves the grip to the socket nor transfers water. Circular couplings compare opposing forward axes and ignore irrelevant wrist roll. Existing port-distance and aligned-dwell gates still determine docking. The tutorial uses one compact board in place of the old status board while active; the old status is hidden rather than stacked underneath. XR tutorial presentation is hidden in desktop preview.

The broad-valve tap alternative now allows at most 12 degrees of wrist rotation during a fresh pinch-and-release, replacing the historical five-degree tolerance. A normal 45-degree turn remains available. A larger incomplete turn keeps the previous detent. Docking or proximity never fills a tank: the accepted open-valve transfer or a complete primed creek stroke still owns all water accounting.

Tool grip contact uses the thumb/index fingertip midpoint, matching the car workshop grab reference, instead of the palm midpoint. Existing aiming and ballistic behavior remain for this iteration. The car SDK HandVisual mesh and skeleton are reused. A depth-tested Emberdeep material clips hand pixels inside up to 12 explicitly inscribed solid boxes; it does not move tracked hands, solve physical finger collisions or author grasp poses. Parts outside those solid interiors remain visible. The original soft-alpha flame contour and response to accepted water are restored; the effect must not become an opaque triangular card.

Both complete left/right scene-wiring cases are included in the 40 passes. Quest and PICO APKs were built with version 0.2.3/code 6, zero errors and exactly the camp/fireground scene whitelist. Both builds restored all 28 audited configuration hashes; 77 verified source and scene files also remained unchanged. Quest 3 installation/version is verified, but STANDBY persisted and no app process was observed after wake/launch requests. Worn-headset acceptance remains pending. Final release evidence is assembled at Logs/EmberdeepPolish/ReleaseEvidence.json. No Plastic upload, check-in or publication is implied.

The SDK already used normal LEqual hand depth testing; this iteration must not claim an existing x-ray shader was the diagnosed cause. Interior clipping is an additional explicit rendering safeguard. No general physical nonpenetrating hand or automatic finger wrap is delivered. Hardware occlusion, pose comfort and stereo quality remain device checks.

pages.title: 0.2.3 Device Handoff and Evidence Boundary
pages.intro: Historical 0.2.3 handoff. At that time front menu placement was the only narrowly recorded positive user confirmation. The user later confirmed normal hand following in 0.2.4; current 0.2.5 requires separate checks on PICO 4 and Quest 3.

items: Aim using a relaxed hand and pinch without losing the target. Verify no always-on duplicate ray, no click by the other hand, no offscreen target selection and no held-pinch click-through.

Approach the hydrant from varied wrist rolls. Follow every cue without extra instructions. Check that guidance preserves grip contact and that alignment/proximity alone grants no water. Repeat the 12-degree tap alternative and a full turn; partial turns beyond tolerance must not toggle.
Use the creek intake and complete pump stroke. Cover a hand or pause during each action. Verify safe stop, discarded incomplete work and deliberate fresh rearm.

Inspect tool grip at the thumb/index midpoint. Move hands around and inside declared solid interiors: hidden portions must not show through, but nearby free fingers and handle openings must remain visible. Record clipping boundaries and tracking loss; do not label this a physical hand collision test.
Inspect broad soft flames, smoke, water hits and extinguishing in both eyes. Record Editor screenshots separately from worn-headset captures and measure actual PICO 4 CPU/GPU frame timing.
Complete menu, manual refill, combat, retained shop/upgrade and sector/retry/camp transitions. M2 safe search, animals, settlement and durable saves remain proposed; this candidate does not add them.
